conventions.convention: The torus acts on the left. Its bundle linearization induces the section action U_t s(x) = ρ_t(t⁻¹x)s(t⁻¹x); the differentials commute with this action.
Principal symbols use the positive-frequency substitution ∂^α ↦ (iξ)^α. Ellipticity of a complex means exactness of its principal-symbol sequence at every nonzero real cotangent vector.

The equivariant index is the alternating cohomology representation in R(T), and its character is the alternating trace. Finite-dimensional cohomology is required in the definition; transversally elliptic distributional indices are excluded.

Heat kernels are relative to Riemannian volume. The tangent kernel uses inverse Fourier normalization (2π)⁻ⁿ and has integral I. The principal symbol may be matrix-valued, provided it is Hermitian and uniformly positive quadratic.
A simple fixed point has invertible I − dg_x. Its contribution uses the absolute real determinant; in dimension zero this is the empty determinant 1.
The general fixed-component formula assumes full AC. The separate isolated-point heat branch assumes only countable choice together with the explicitly stated spectral and Hodge hypotheses.

Cotangent integration uses the orientation (dθ)ⁿ/n!, with θ = Σ ξ_j dx_j. The character is the eigenvalue-weighted relative compact-support Chern character, and the normal denominator is the full character of λ₋₁(ν_C*), rather than only its rank or determinant.
The sphere has outward orientation. The bundle action on differential forms induces inverse pullback on sections, and the normalized invariant area form has integral 1.

load_bearing.statement: For the specified equivariant elliptic complex with finite-dimensional cohomology, Ind_T(E•) := Σ_j (−1)^j[H^j(E•)] ∈ R(T), and χ_E•(t) := Σ_j (−1)^j tr(U_t^j|H^j(E•)).

Assume countable choice. For a smooth second-order operator on a finite-rank Hermitian bundle over a compact boundaryless Riemannian manifold, with Hermitian principal symbol p(x,ξ) ≥ c|ξ|²I and the stated nonnegative selfadjoint spectral realization and smooth heat kernel, k_x(w) = (2π)⁻ⁿ∫ exp(iw·ξ)exp(−p(x,ξ)) dξ is Schwartz, ∫k_x = I, and t^(n/2)K_t(exp_x(√t a),exp_x(√t b)) → k_x(a−b), locally uniformly for bounded a,b. For every integer L > n, ‖K_t(y,z)‖ ≤ C_L t^(−n/2)(1+d(y,z)/√t)^(−L) for 0 < t ≤ 1. Dimension zero has the stated fiberwise finite-dimensional limit.

Assume countable choice. For the specified unitary equivariant first-order elliptic complex on a compact boundaryless Riemannian manifold, with the stated selfadjoint Hodge spectral and heat data and harmonic representatives, if every fixed point of g is simple, then lim_(t↓0) Str(U_g exp(−tΔ)) = Σ_(x∈M^g) [Σ_j (−1)^j tr(ρ_g^j|E_x^j)]/|det_R(I−dg_x)|.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit choice assumption inherited by Fourier inversion, smooth partitions, the isolated heat argument, and sphere cohomology.
The full-choice background of the general analytic-symbol and fixed-component formula.
Polynomial-weighted derivative bounds defining the tangent heat kernel's Schwartz regularity.
Fourier reconstruction and normalization ∫k_x = I, after converting the supplier's 2π convention.
Uniform Schwartz bounds for the inverse transform of the positive matrix-symbol exponential.
The finite-chart frozen-coefficient heat parametrix and its cutoffs.
Absolutely integrable Fourier and Volterra kernel calculations; no undamped double Fourier integral is exchanged.
Passing to tangent-kernel limits and integrating the rescaled fixed-point density under an explicit integrable polynomial majorant.
The real cohomology dimensions of S²; the example separately explains complexification and the torus action.
The normalized sphere area form is not exact because its integral is nonzero and the sphere has empty boundary.

seams_checked.note: Checked the compact-symbol definition and all three symbol lemmas against the character theorem's F2, L1–L3 and Proof 1.1–4.1. The real-normal embedding, S_g localization, eigenvalue weighting, full normal denominator, and dθ orientation agree. The general formula uses the suppliers' full AC hypothesis.

Checked the Borel theorem and the fixed-locus/slice suppliers. Borel localization concerns ordinary rational or real Borel cohomology and M^T; it is not used as a replacement for compact-support K-theory localization at g. The character theorem correctly obtains M^g reconstruction from its separate symbol supplier and explicitly distinguishes trace weighting from Borel rank.
